blocks.content: Eustatic changes represent global variations in sea level caused by alterations in the total volume of ocean water or changes in the capacity of ocean basins.

rows: Glacial melt/freezing, thermal expansion, ocean basin volume changes
Tectonic forces, crustal loading/unloading (glacio-isostasy), sediment deposition
Affects sea level uniformly across connected global oceans
Varies locally based on crustal uplift or subsidence rates
Reversible via post-glacial rebound or tectonic relaxation

items: Distinguish between Eustatic (global/volume/basin capacity) and Isostatic (local/tectonic/crustal uplift or subsidence) changes.
Identify geomorphic evidence of emergent coasts (raised beaches, wave-cut cliffs) vs. submergent coasts (rias, fjords, dalmatian coasts).
Note the impact of the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) when global sea level was approximately 120 to 130 meters lower than present levels.
Indian geography contexts often test submerged coastal features such as the ancient port city of Dwarka and Gulf of Khambhat structures.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Eustatic changes are global variations in sea level caused by alterations in the total volume of ocean water or changes in the capacity of ocean basins.
Isostatic changes refer to localized sea-level variations caused by the vertical movement (uplift or subsidence) of the Earth's crust.
Glacial-interglacial cycles during the Quaternary period caused dramatic worldwide fluctuations in sea level.
Evidence of sea-level fall includes raised beaches, marine terraces, and elevated wave-cut platforms.
Evidence of sea-level rise includes submerged forests, drowned river valleys (rias), fjords, and submerged historical structures like ancient Dwarka.
Modern sea-level rise is primarily driven by thermal expansion of warming ocean water and the melting of ice sheets and glaciers.
